correctness.rationale: Torsion of an idempotent vanishes exactly when image and kernel are subalgebras. Splitting almost-Abelian subalgebras by whether their projection onto Ke is nonzero yields three disjoint cases. For odd characteristic A=diag(I_n,−I_n), invariant subspaces split by eigenspace and the deficient-hyperplane pair count is T_(n,t); lift count is (q−1)q^(2n). For char2 A=I and bracket lies in span(x,y), so every idempotent works. Gaussian exponent bounds yield log_q H=3n²/2+O_q(n). Independent n=1,q=3 substitution gives rank counts 1,63,63,1. General almost-Abelian precedent proves the framework; special enumeration checked, not assumed from its abstract.
residual_risks: Published general almost-Abelian rank spectrum provides the full template; the submission must credit it prominently. A future reviewer may regard repeated-eigenspace T evaluation and rarity exponent as mechanical corollaries rather than independent novelty.
